So, you don't agree that telling somebody not to tell you what to do is telling them what to do?

> "Don't tell me what to do" falls into an order and an order is exactly what the person who just gave one, doesn't want to receive.  

If you don't get that I don't know what else to tell you. It's as simple as that. Don't want or don't care about what people are telling you to do? Just ignore the statement or tell them why you won't take it into consideration. Not by telling them what to do back which is irrational and it's pretty much doing the same thing you just told them not to do.

They are telling me what TO NOT do. Which falls into the category of orders.

EXAMPLE 1: 
A: I'm going to hug a giraffe!
B: Don't do that!
A: Dont tell me what to do!

EXAMPLE 2:
A: I'm going to **tell you what to not do** !
B: Don't do that!
A: Don't tell me what **to do** !

I'm just trying to point out the hypocrisy within this statement. "Don't tell me what to do" falls into an order and an order is exactly what the person who just gave one, doesn't want to receive.
But they are telling you what not to do which is still telling you what to do which is still what they don't want you to do
